paragraphs: In reinforcement learning, a useful notion of state similarity should reflect what an agent can achieve from those states. Bisimulation metrics provide this connection within a single Markov decision process: nearby states have similar optimal values. Extending that reasoning across different processes would help analyze situations such as transferring a policy between environments.

The paper establishes a generalized bisimulation metric for pairs of processes and proves three mathematical properties: symmetry, a triangle inequality across processes, and a distance bound for identical states. These properties give the cross-environment comparison a rigorous foundation and support further analysis beyond simply defining a similarity score.

Using this foundation, the authors derive explicit bounds for policy transfer, state aggregation, and estimation from samples. They report that these bounds are strictly tighter than corresponding bounds from standard bisimulation metrics. They also provide a closed-form sample complexity result, making estimation requirements more explicit than previous asymptotic results. Numerical experiments support the theory and the metric’s usefulness across multiple processes.
neurips-2025-a-generalized-bisimulation-.tldr: A rigorously established cross-environment state similarity metric yields tighter theoretical bounds for reinforcement learning transfer, aggregation, and estimation.

paragraphs: Mixture-of-Experts language models save computation by sending each input to only some of their experts. Training commonly includes a load balancing objective so that work is distributed across experts. The authors observe that this objective can also produce overlapping experts and routing that is too uniform, weakening specialization during post-training.

Their method adds two complementary training objectives. An orthogonality loss encourages experts to handle distinct token types, while a variance loss encourages the router to make more discriminating choices. Together, these objectives aim to preserve useful differences between experts while retaining the existing mechanism for balancing their workload. Gradient analysis shows that the new objectives are compatible with that mechanism.

Experiments across several architectures and benchmarks show improved expert specialization, with improvements over classic MoE baselines reaching up to 23.79%. The method also maintains load balancing on downstream tasks. Its practical appeal is that these changes operate through training objectives and require neither architectural modifications nor additional model components.
neurips-2025-advancing-expert-specializa.tldr: Two added training objectives improve MoE expert specialization while preserving load balancing and leaving the architecture unchanged.

paragraphs: Audio super-resolution produces a higher-resolution waveform from a lower-resolution recording. This paper argues that earlier generative approaches do not make enough use of the information already present in the input. Its system compresses waveforms into a continuous latent space and learns a bridge from the low-resolution representation to the high-resolution representation.

This construction makes the generation process correspond directly to the desired audio transformation. To improve training when high-resolution examples are limited, the authors also provide the source and target frequencies as inputs. This frequency-aware version learns different upsampling relationships within training. Cascaded bridges and two prior augmentation strategies then support successive upsampling stages and greater flexibility in audio post-production.

Across speech, general audio, and music evaluations, the authors report state-of-the-art objective and perceptual quality for upsampling to 48 kHz. They also report the first results for their any-to-192 kHz audio super-resolution setting. The contribution therefore combines stronger use of the original recording with a framework for multiple target resolutions and cascaded processing.
neurips-2025-audio-super-resolution-with.tldr: Latent bridge models use the input recording to guide audio super-resolution, supporting frequency-aware training and cascaded upsampling to 192 kHz.

paragraphs: Recovering human movement from video becomes especially difficult when the camera also moves. Applications that need motion in world coordinates must distinguish the person’s movement through the environment from changes caused by the camera. BEDLAM2.0 addresses a training-data shortage for this problem by providing synthetic videos with known human and camera motion.

The dataset expands BEDLAM with more varied and realistic cameras and camera trajectories. It also increases the diversity and realism of body shapes, movements, clothing, hair, and surrounding 3D environments, and introduces shoes. These changes broaden the visual and motion conditions available for training models that estimate human pose and movement.

The authors compare state-of-the-art methods trained on the original and updated datasets and report significantly better accuracy with BEDLAM2.0, particularly for estimating people in world coordinates. For research use, they provide rendered videos, body parameters, and camera motion annotations. They also supply 3D assets where they hold the necessary rights and links to third-party assets.
neurips-2025-bedlam2-0-synthetic-humans-.tldr: BEDLAM2.0 expands synthetic human and camera motion data and improves training for reconstructing human movement in world coordinates.

paragraphs: Strategic classification studies decisions in settings where people or organizations change their features to obtain favorable outcomes. A classifier must therefore account for responses to its decision rule. The paper investigates how pretrained language models can support this process as datasets and the number of participating individuals grow.

The proposed method, GLIM, uses in-context learning without fine-tuning the language model. During a forward pass, its self-attention process implicitly simulates the two linked parts of strategic classification: feature manipulation and optimization of the decision rule. This gradient-free approach is intended to make adaptation to changing strategic environments more economical.

The authors provide a theoretical result showing that GLIM can help pretrained language models adapt to a broad range of strategic manipulations. Experiments with several pretrained models on real and synthetic financial and internet datasets demonstrate robustness and efficiency. The contribution is a way to use existing model capabilities for strategic decision-making without repeatedly updating model weights, supported by both theoretical analysis and empirical evaluation.
neurips-2025-breaking-the-gradient-barri.tldr: GLIM uses pretrained language models and in-context learning to handle strategic classification without gradient-based fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Language-model agents are software systems that themselves need maintenance as bugs appear and requirements change. Software engineering agents have shown promise on conventional software, but this paper asks whether that capability carries over to repairing agent systems. Its focus includes both bug reports and feature requests from real projects.

The authors first manually examine 201 issues to identify recurring categories. They then construct AgentIssue-bench, a reproducible collection of 50 repair tasks, investing 500 person-hours in the process. Each task includes an executable environment and tests that trigger the failure, making it possible to evaluate whether a proposed change resolves the issue.

Evaluations of state-of-the-art software engineering agents produce resolution rates of only 0.67% to 4.67%. These results show limited effectiveness on the benchmark and motivate more work on tools for maintaining agent systems. The paper contributes both an organized account of real maintenance problems and a testable evaluation setting in which progress on those problems can be measured.
neurips-2025-can-agent-fix-agent-issues-.tldr: A benchmark of real agent-system issues finds that current software engineering agents resolve only a small fraction of the tested tasks.

paragraphs: In many tabular prediction problems, the outcomes that matter most occur much less often than other outcomes. Class-imbalanced learning addresses this uneven distribution. CLIMB provides a shared benchmark for studying these methods across different application domains and levels of imbalance, allowing comparisons beyond a single dataset or setting.

The benchmark brings together 73 real-world datasets and unified implementations of 29 representative algorithms. Its Python package supplies a common interface, documentation, and code quality controls. This shared implementation framework makes methods easier to apply and compare, while the dataset collection exposes them to a range of practical data conditions.

The experimental analysis considers both predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Its findings highlight weaknesses of naive rebalancing, the effectiveness of ensembles, and the importance of data quality. These are practical observations from the benchmark rather than a claim that one approach always wins. The paper’s main contribution is an evaluation resource that connects method comparisons with guidance about the factors influencing their performance.
neurips-2025-climb-class-imbalanced-lear.tldr: CLIMB compares 29 class-imbalanced learning algorithms across 73 tabular datasets and identifies practical lessons about ensembles, rebalancing, and data quality.

paragraphs: Autonomous-driving perception systems must cope with changing conditions at deployment. Test-time adaptation can help, but optimization for 3D object detection may be unstable. Combining adapted model checkpoints offers another route to stability, although existing merging approaches can require expensive checkpoint access and repeated forward passes.

CodeMerge makes merging decisions using compact representations of checkpoints. It derives a low-dimensional fingerprint for each checkpoint from the source model’s penultimate features and stores these representations in a key-value codebook. Ridge leverage scores computed from the fingerprints determine the merging coefficients, reducing the overhead associated with working directly with full models during this process.

The authors report a 14.9% NDS improvement for end-to-end detection on nuScenes-C and an improvement exceeding 7.6% mAP for LiDAR detection on nuScenes-to-KITTI. They also report benefits for online mapping, motion prediction, and planning without training those downstream tasks. The findings support compact checkpoint representations as a practical basis for model composition that preserves adaptation quality while reducing computational demands.
neurips-2025-codemerge-codebook-guided-m.tldr: CodeMerge uses compact checkpoint fingerprints to guide efficient model merging for more robust 3D perception under changing deployment conditions.

paragraphs: Pursuit-evasion games model opponents moving through a graph while trying to catch or escape one another. Changing the graph often forces existing reinforcement learning methods to recompute or fine-tune their policies. Equilibrium Policy Generalization aims to train policies that work on unseen graphs without this additional adaptation.

The framework trains across graph structures against an equilibrium policy for each graph. A dynamic programming algorithm supplies these reference policies and is proven to generate pure-strategy Nash equilibria with near-optimal time complexity. To scale with the number of pursuers, the authors add grouping to dynamic programming and use a sequence model to decompose joint policies.

The framework covers both pursuers and evaders in settings with no exits or multiple exits. Experiments combining equilibrium guidance with a cross-graph distance feature show desirable zero-shot performance on unseen real-world graphs. With an additional equilibrium heuristic for graphs containing exits, the generalized pursuer policy can match fine-tuned policies from state-of-the-art methods. That matching result is specific to the stated training setting.
neurips-2025-equilibrium-policy-generali.tldr: Training against graph-specific equilibrium policies enables pursuit-evasion policies to transfer to unseen graphs without fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Multilingual language-model training requires choosing how much data to allocate to each language. This is difficult because languages interact during learning, and useful proportions depend on the scale of the dataset. CLIMB approaches allocation by explicitly accounting for those interactions when measuring how much training support each language effectively receives.

Its central quantity is an interaction-aware language ratio that incorporates dependencies between languages. The framework then uses a two-step optimization procedure: it first equalizes marginal benefits across languages, then maximizes the magnitude of the resulting allocation vectors. This structure makes a complicated joint allocation problem more manageable while keeping cross-language effects within the calculation.

Experiments show that CLIMB can accurately measure interactions in multiple multilingual settings. Models trained with its chosen proportions consistently achieve state-of-the-art multilingual performance in the reported evaluations and are competitive with open-source models trained on more tokens. The findings suggest that carefully selecting the language mixture can improve the value of a training corpus, alongside decisions about its overall size.
neurips-2025-exploring-polyglot-harmony-.tldr: CLIMB optimizes multilingual training proportions by modeling cross-language interactions and balancing the benefits of additional data.

paragraphs: A response can address a user’s topic while still violating explicit output requirements. This paper studies precise instruction following, where compliance can be checked directly. The authors find that most models overfit to a small collection of constraints used in existing benchmarks and struggle when evaluated on unfamiliar types of requirements.

To measure that generalization gap, they introduce IFBench with 58 new, diverse, challenging constraints outside the familiar benchmark set. The benchmark shifts attention toward whether a model can follow previously unseen requirements. The authors also investigate training methods and data choices that could improve this ability, rather than treating evaluation performance as the only contribution.

Their training approach uses carefully designed verification modules to provide rewards for reinforcement learning. They show that reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards significantly improves instruction following. Alongside IFBench, they release 29 additional hand-annotated training constraints, verification functions, training prompts, and code. Together, these resources support evaluating generalization and developing training procedures with directly checkable feedback.
neurips-2025-generalizing-verifiable-ins.tldr: IFBench exposes weak generalization to unfamiliar output constraints, while training with verifiable rewards significantly improves instruction following.

paragraphs: Plasma turbulence impairs confinement in fusion systems, making its simulation important for reactor design. Full nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations evolve a five-dimensional distribution over time and are computationally expensive. Reduced models approximate energy transport more cheaply, but omit nonlinear effects associated with the full dynamics.

GyroSwin is a neural surrogate designed to model those five-dimensional simulations. It extends hierarchical Vision Transformers to five dimensions and adds cross-attention and integration modules connecting three-dimensional electrostatic potential fields with the distribution function. A channelwise separation of modes, inspired by nonlinear physics, provides another component tailored to the underlying problem.

The authors report better heat-flux prediction than widely used reduced numerical models, reproduction of the turbulent energy cascade, and a thousandfold reduction in the cost of fully resolved nonlinear gyrokinetics while retaining physical verifiability. They also report promising scaling behavior in experiments reaching one billion parameters. The results support learning a surrogate for richer plasma dynamics while substantially reducing their computational expense.
neurips-2025-gyroswin-5d-surrogates-for-.tldr: GyroSwin models full five-dimensional plasma turbulence with a neural surrogate that improves heat-flux prediction and greatly reduces simulation cost.

paragraphs: Domain-specific language-model tasks require deciding what expert knowledge to provide and how the model should use it. EGO-Prompt automates refinement of both prompts and reasoning guidance. It starts with a general prompt and a human-created Semantic Causal Graph, while explicitly allowing that initial graph to be incomplete or imperfect.

The method first converts the graph into nearly deterministic reasoning guidance for each input. It then adapts how the language model uses that guidance alongside the original input. An iterative optimization process uses textual gradients with ground-truth feedback to refine both the graph and the reasoning mechanism, accommodating differences in how models benefit from domain knowledge.

On public health, transportation, and human behavior tasks, the authors report F1 improvements of 7.32%–12.61% over leading methods. They also report that smaller models can reach larger-model performance at under 20% of the original cost. The refined domain graph is an additional output, improving interpretability by making the knowledge used to guide reasoning more explicit.
neurips-2025-how-to-auto-optimize-prompt.tldr: EGO-Prompt uses ground-truth feedback to refine expert knowledge graphs and reasoning prompts, improving domain-task performance and efficiency.

paragraphs: Privacy auditing asks what an algorithm’s observable behavior reveals about its privacy protection. Recent approaches make this more computationally efficient by intervening on multiple training examples within one training run. Prior work established that such an audit can lower-bound the algorithm’s true privacy parameter, but left open how close that bound can get.

This paper studies the maximum effectiveness achievable by one-run auditing and how it depends on the algorithm being examined. Its central finding is that the observable effects of different data elements can interfere with one another. Although combining interventions saves training runs, that interference creates a barrier to extracting precise privacy information from the resulting observations.

The authors also present conceptual approaches for reducing this barrier. Their intended role is to improve one-run audits of real machine learning algorithms by making individual effects less difficult to distinguish. The contribution therefore clarifies what limits audit precision and identifies a direction for improvement, without treating a valid lower bound as an exact recovery of the privacy parameter.
neurips-2025-how-well-can-differential-p.tldr: The paper characterizes one-run privacy auditing limits and identifies interference between data elements’ observable effects as the central barrier.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning depends on which questions the model practices. The authors show that most existing methods provably fail to learn from questions on which the model always succeeds or always fails. This creates a need to find questions that offer useful training signals as the model’s capabilities change.

LILO prioritizes questions with high variance in success, a quantity the paper calls learnability. These are questions for which the model’s outcomes vary, giving training something to distinguish between. The authors provide a theoretical result that LILO maximizes expected model improvement and investigate ways to identify highly learnable questions efficiently.

Across multiple starting models, training algorithms, and reasoning datasets, LILO consistently improves final test accuracy. It can also reduce by a factor of three the training steps needed to reach that accuracy. The paper discusses extending learnability toward agents that expand their capabilities autonomously, but that broader possibility is presented as a future direction beyond the reported training experiments.
neurips-2025-lilo-learning-to-reason-at-.tldr: LILO selects reasoning questions with variable success outcomes to improve learning efficiency and final accuracy.

paragraphs: Masked diffusion models generate discrete outputs through a process governed by a masking schedule. This paper gives that process an interpretation through energy minimization in discrete optimal transport. The aim is to connect the model’s theoretical structure with practical choices about how generation progresses.

The authors prove that kinetic, conditional kinetic, and geodesic energy formulations are mathematically equivalent under the structure of masked diffusion models. They further show that the models minimize all three when the mask schedule meets a closed-form optimality condition. The schedule condition is essential to this minimization result; the equivalence does not make every possible schedule optimal.

The theory motivates a practical schedule family parameterized by Beta distributions. This turns schedule selection into a two-dimensional search that can be performed after training without modifying the model. On synthetic and real-world benchmarks, these energy-inspired schedules outperform handcrafted alternatives, especially when sampling uses few steps. The findings link a formal account of generation to an inexpensive way of improving its execution.
neurips-2025-masked-diffusion-models-as-.tldr: An energy-minimization theory for masked diffusion motivates post-training schedule tuning that improves sampling, particularly with few steps.

paragraphs: Explaining a time-series classifier requires identifying which parts of a signal influence its decision. Existing post-hoc methods often examine only the time domain from one perspective. MIX expands the explanation process to multiple time-frequency views at different resolutions, constructed with the Haar Discrete Wavelet Transform.

The framework lets information from an explanation in one view refine explanations in other views. A greedy selection procedure searches these views for informative features aligned with a user’s preferred perspective. Its OSIGV mechanism assigns importance to segments through overlapping windows, while keystone-first IG uses information from another view to refine attribution within a given view.

These components connect explanations across representations instead of treating each representation as an isolated account of the prediction. Experiments spanning multiple time-series benchmarks and model architectures show significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods in explanation faithfulness and robustness. The contribution concerns how well explanations reflect model decisions and remain reliable, rather than a reported improvement in the classifier’s predictive accuracy.
neurips-2025-mix-a-multi-view-time-frequ.tldr: MIX combines interacting time-frequency views to produce more faithful and robust explanations of time-series classifier decisions.

paragraphs: Gaussian splatting reconstruction usually depends on supplied camera poses, but estimating those poses can be unreliable in textureless rooms. Existing approaches without pose inputs can also struggle with abrupt camera movement. NopeRoomGS addresses these issues by building local reconstructions first and then combining them into a global scene.

For short video clips, a lightweight neural geometric representation initializes local 3D Gaussians. Multi-frame tracking constraints and depth priors from a foundation model help stabilize this stage. The global stage then fuses the local reconstructions and alternates optimization of camera poses and Gaussian parameters, reducing interference between their gradients while refining both.

The framework additionally decomposes camera-pose optimization using a piecewise planarity assumption to improve robustness to abrupt motion. That assumption is part of its approach to indoor geometry. Experiments on Replica, ScanNet, and Tanks & Temples report state-of-the-art camera-pose estimation and novel-view synthesis. The method thus removes the need for camera poses as inputs while estimating them within the reconstruction process.
neurips-2025-noperoomgs-indoor-3d-gaussi.tldr: NopeRoomGS reconstructs indoor scenes without input camera poses by combining locally initialized Gaussians with alternating global refinement.

paragraphs: An embodied agent sees objects from changing viewpoints, often observing only part of an object in any one frame. AutoSeg3D treats online 3D segmentation as tracking object instances over time. This addresses a weakness of pipelines that emphasize spatial interactions while making limited use of temporal identity.

Object queries carry information between observations. Long-term association maintains coherent object identities and features, while short-term updates incorporate the latest view. Spatial consistency learning also reduces the fragmentation inherited from vision foundation model outputs. Together, these mechanisms help assemble a more complete understanding from partial observations without requiring dense temporal interactions across entire point clouds.

The authors report state-of-the-art results, including an improvement of 2.8 AP over ESAM on ScanNet200 and consistent gains on ScanNet, SceneNN, and 3RScan. These findings support identity-aware temporal reasoning as an important component of online segmentation. The approach connects efficiency with perception quality by concentrating information exchange in sparse object queries while using observations accumulated over time.
neurips-2025-online-segment-any-3d-thing.tldr: AutoSeg3D improves online 3D segmentation by tracking object identities and combining partial observations over time.

paragraphs: Graph unlearning aims to remove information from a trained graph neural network without paying the full cost of retraining. The task is complicated by graph structure and recursive message passing, which connect information across the data. Different downstream tasks and deletion requests further broaden the conditions an unlearning method must handle.

OpenGU supplies a common evaluation framework for these conditions. It integrates 16 state-of-the-art unlearning algorithms, 37 datasets from multiple domains, and 13 graph neural network backbones. The benchmark supports combinations of downstream tasks and flexible unlearning requests, addressing inconsistencies caused by comparing methods in separate, less adaptable evaluation setups.

The authors conduct extensive experiments and report ten conclusions about existing methods, including insights into their limitations and directions for further research. The abstract does not enumerate those conclusions, so the concrete contribution here is the breadth and flexibility of the comparison framework. OpenGU enables researchers to investigate how unlearning behavior changes across methods, datasets, model architectures, tasks, and requests.
neurips-2025-opengu-a-comprehensive-benc.tldr: OpenGU provides a unified, flexible benchmark for comparing graph unlearning across algorithms, datasets, model backbones, and deletion requests.

paragraphs: Locating an object from a language description becomes harder when the relevant scene is unknown. This paper introduces Cross-Scene Spatial Reasoning and Grounding, where the target may appear anywhere in a collection of 3D scenes. The task requires both finding promising scenes and identifying the described object within them.

The proposed CoRe framework separates those operations into matching followed by grounding. Its text-scene alignment module learns global scene representations for retrieving candidate scenes from the description. A second module builds detailed associations between words and objects, filtering redundant context to support precise object-level reasoning. This organization addresses both exhaustive-search costs and the difficulty of aligning language with spatial information.

The authors also introduce CrossScene-RETR and an evaluation protocol for the new task. Across four multimodal datasets, CoRe substantially reduces computational overhead while outperforming compared methods in scene retrieval and object grounding. The findings support using coarse scene selection together with fine-grained object reasoning to handle language-guided searches across a larger scene archive.
neurips-2025-robust-cross-modal-alignmen.tldr: CoRe retrieves candidate 3D scenes before locating described objects, improving cross-scene grounding while reducing computation.

paragraphs: Gaussian splatting renders scenes efficiently, but simplifying the thickness and overlap of its primitives can produce incorrect depth ordering. Those errors can appear as popping artifacts. SAP changes the representation so that the primitives generated for each viewpoint lie parallel to the image plane, making ordering easier to handle correctly.

Because the primitives are parallel within a view, one global sorting operation is sufficient to obtain correct depth ordering at every pixel. The framework combines view-specific two-dimensional primitives with an efficient decoder that maintains three-dimensional consistency. This pairing connects a convenient rendering representation to a coherent reconstruction of the underlying scene.

The authors also show that primitive function values remain consistent between view space and screen space. Within their framework, this permits arbitrary radial basis functions without projection errors. Experiments on diverse datasets report state-of-the-art rendering quality at real-time speed. The central contribution is a representation whose geometry supports exact sorting while retaining efficient rendering and consistency across viewpoints.
neurips-2025-sap-exact-sorting-in-splatt.tldr: SAP uses screen-aligned primitives so one global sort provides correct per-pixel depth ordering for high-quality real-time rendering.

paragraphs: Compressing a language model’s key-value cache saves resources during long-context inference, but discarding token information creates two problems. A token’s importance can change during generation, making irreversible eviction poorly matched to later attention. Also, many individually marginal tokens can collectively matter, even if each appears safe to remove.

SmallKV uses a smaller model to compensate for these losses, drawing on similarity between attention matrices in models of different sizes. It maintains attention matching so that the smaller model helps the larger one perceive globally important information. It also uses the smaller model’s attention scores to approximate the larger model’s scores for marginal tokens.

Experiments on GSM8K, BBH, MT-Bench, and LongBench demonstrate the method’s effectiveness. Efficiency evaluations report throughput between 1.75 and 2.56 times that of baseline methods. The contribution is a way to support cache compression with an auxiliary source of attention information, addressing both changing token importance and the cumulative value of weaker signals rather than relying solely on eviction decisions.
neurips-2025-smallkv-small-model-assiste.tldr: SmallKV uses a smaller model’s attention to compensate for information lost during large-model cache compression and improve inference throughput.

paragraphs: A 360-degree image is often split into perspective patches to avoid projection distortion during depth estimation. Processing those patches independently can give them inconsistent depth scales. ST²360D instead arranges perspective views into a video-like sequence, allowing an existing video depth model’s temporal consistency to encourage spatial agreement around the panorama.

The pipeline generates perspective frames, predicts their depth with a video model, and merges the results into a complete panoramic depth map. Spherical-uniform sampling distributes views across the sphere while avoiding excessive sampling near the poles. Latitude-guided scanning then orders the frames coherently, beginning around the equator and progressing toward higher latitudes.

This conversion lets the method use capabilities already present in video depth estimation without additional training. Experiments demonstrate strong zero-shot performance across several datasets and support for resolutions up to 4K. The contribution is the organization of a single panoramic image into a sequence that makes temporal modeling useful for reconciling depth estimates across different viewing directions.
neurips-2025-st-2-360d-spatial-to-tempor.tldr: ST²360D turns panoramic views into a video-like sequence to obtain consistent 360-degree depth estimates without additional training.

paragraphs: Spectral clustering partitions graphs using eigenvector information, but computing that information becomes costly on massive graphs. Sparsification reduces the number of edges while retaining useful spectral structure. Classical methods choose edges according to effective resistance, which itself requires expensive preprocessing. This paper asks when simple uniform edge sampling can suffice.

The main guarantee applies to graphs with strongly separated clusters, expressed through a large structure ratio. Under this condition, sampling O(γ² n log n / ε²) edges preserves the spectral structure needed for clustering, where γ is the Laplacian condition number. The proof establishes approximate orthogonality between a dominant eigenspace of the sparsifier and the cluster indicators, keeping the resulting embedding faithful.

The analysis develops resistance bounds for edges within clusters, a restricted-rank effective resistance formulation, and a matrix concentration bound adapted to the relevant eigenspace. These tools remove the need for importance sampling in the stated setting. The result shows that uniform sampling can preserve clustering structure under strong clusterability, rather than establishing that it works for arbitrary graphs.
neurips-2025-structure-aware-spectral-sp.tldr: For strongly clusterable graphs, uniform edge sampling can provably preserve the spectral structure needed for clustering without resistance-based sampling.
